extracted.intended_audience: AAAI authors and reviewers (authors with accepted papers for AAAI Press/AAAI-related publications; conference reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Official AAAI policies and guidelines governing authorship, permitted use of AI systems, reviewer confidentiality and responsibilities, and procedural requirements (author kits, ethics, copyright requests, errata) for papers published by AAAI Press and AAAI-affiliated venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on use of AI systems in producing AAAI publications
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is AAAI’s policy that any AI system, including Generative Models such as Chat‑GPT, BARD, and DALL‑E, does not satisfy the criteria for authorship of papers published by AAAI and, as such, also cannot be used as a citable source in papers published by AAAI.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI systems cannot be listed as authors or cited as sources. Attribution of authorship carries accountability which cannot be effectively applied to AI systems. Examples listed explicitly include generative models (Chat‑GPT, BARD, DALL‑E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of AI system use in manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: “The use of any AI system in the development of an AAAI-affiliated publication is only allowed if its role is properly documented in the manuscript.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors used AI tools (e.g., for drafting, figure generation, data augmentation), they must clearly describe the tool's role in the manuscript. All human authors remain fully responsible for the entire content (text, figures, references, appendices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' responsibility for content
rubrics_metrics.description: “Ultimately, all authors are responsible for the entire content of their papers, including text, figures, references, and appendices.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when AI tools are used and documented, the named human authors bear full accountability and must ensure accuracy, originality, and compliance with policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidentiality and prohibition on uploading submissions to untrusted systems
rubrics_metrics.description: “All conference submissions have to be kept confidential. Because of this, submitted papers cannot be uploaded into any system that does not ensure that they are not shared with others. This includes also prompting Large Language Models with papers or parts of them, because these systems may disclose part of the prompt to other users.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not upload submissions or parts of them to external platforms (including LLM services) that could retain or disclose content. The policy treats such uploads as breaches of confidentiality due to potential prompt/data leakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibility for review content and limits on tools
rubrics_metrics.description: “Reviewers ... are fully responsible for the entire content of their reviews, so tools can be used to improve the wording of the review but not to generate its content.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may use tools (e.g., grammar/style aids) to edit phrasing, but must not use tools to produce substantive judgments, evaluations, or factual assertions in place of their own analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author instructions / author kit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of AAAI Press monographs, edited collections, and AI Magazine authors should consult the instructions on the AAAI Press and AI Magazine Web pages and download the author kit for their specific conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors with accepted papers should obtain the author kit whose URL appears in the acceptance letter; follow the kit for formatting, submission, and publication procedures specific to the venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with AAAI Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement and Publication Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAAI Publications Ethics and Malpractice Statement (current version updated July 2024) and the AAAI Publication Policy (version approved May 8, 2017) apply to AAAI publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and contributors must follow the detailed ethical/malpractice and publication policies linked on the page; consult those documents for requirements on misconduct, conflicts of interest, duplicate submission, authorship disputes, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request procedure for reproducing copyrighted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducing Copyright Materials: Request Form to Reproduce Copyright Materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reproducing third‑party copyrighted material in an AAAI publication, authors must use the designated request form and follow AAAI’s copyright reproduction procedures (link provided on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Erratum/errata submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: How to submit an erratum or errata to a previously published paper in the AAAI digital Library (current version updated November 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For post-publication corrections, authors should follow the linked erratum submission instructions to have corrections recorded in the AAAI Digital Library.
